questions.stem: Which of the nerves passes from the superior part of the superior orbital fissure?
questions.solutionHtml:
4th nerve
  • The superior orbital fissure is divided into three parts by the annulus of Zinn. The superior part is crossed by Lacrimal N, Frontal N, Trochlear N, and the superior ophthalmic vein.
  • The superior orbital fissure is divided into three parts by the annulus of Zinn.
  • The superior part is crossed by Lacrimal N, Frontal N, Trochlear N, and the superior ophthalmic vein.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old male presents to the emergency department with bruises over his left eye after getting in a fight. On examination, the superior gaze was restricted. A fracture of the orbital floor is suspected. Which of the statements is false regarding the anatomy of orbit?

options.label: A
options.text: The orbit is divided into four self-contained spaces

options.label: B
options.text: The greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid bone bound the superior orbital fissure.

options.label: C
options.text: Ophthalmic artery passes through the superior orbital fissure

options.label: D
options.text: The optic foramen is situated between the lesser wing and body of the sphenoid bone.

questions.answerText: Ophthalmic artery passes through the superior orbital fissure
questions.solutionHtml:
Ophthalmic artery passes through the superior orbital fissure
  • The ophthalmic artery passes through the optic foramen along with its sympathetic plexus, and optic nerve.
  • The superior orbital fissure transmits the oculomotor nerve (superior and inferior divisions), abducens nerve, nasociliary nerve, lacrimal nerve, frontal nerve (all three are branches of the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve), the trochlear nerve, and also the superior ophthalmic vein and branch of the inferior ophthalmic vein.


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 433

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect regarding the anatomy of the orbit?

options.label: A
options.text: The optic foramen is bounded by the greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid bone

options.label: B
options.text: The dural sheath of the optic nerve is adherent to the optic foramen

options.label: C
options.text: The recti muscles originate from the annulus of Zinn.

options.label: D
options.text: The orbit is divided into four self-contained spaces

questions.answerText: The optic foramen is bounded by the greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid bone
questions.solutionHtml:
The optic foramen is bounded by the greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid bone

The optic foramen is situated between the lesser wing and the body of the sphenoid bone.
The orbit is divided into four self-contained spaces, namely (from outside to inside) the subperiosteal space, the peripheral orbital space, the central intraconal space, and the Tenon space.



Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 433

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man complains of sudden onset pain and swelling of the lids. On examination, the lid is oedematous with raised temperature and tenderness. Visual acuity is normal. Which of the following is true about spaces around the orbit?

options.label: A
options.text: Peripheral orbital space is enclosed by extraocular muscles

options.label: B
options.text: The central space is present between the periorbita and extraocular muscles.

options.label: C
options.text: Tenon's space forms the central intraconal space.

options.label: D
options.text: Subperiosteal space is between the bones of the orbital wall and periorbital

questions.answerText: Subperiosteal space is between the bones of the orbital wall and periorbital
questions.solutionHtml:
Subperiosteal space is between the bones of the orbital wall and periorbital

The clinical picture represents a case of Preseptal cellulitis, a bacterial infection of the eyelid anterior to the orbital septum and is due to trauma or the spread of infection from surrounding structures. Patients complain of acute onset pain and swelling of the lids.



Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 433

questions.stemHtml: Which is the following is the incorrect pair in the image ?
questions.solutionHtml:
C = Oculomotor nerve
  • The label C represents the trochlear nerve and not oculomotor nerve.
  • The third, fourth, and sixth cranial nerves innervate the extraocular muscles that position the globes in the orbits. Extraocular muscle paralysis resulting from lesions in one or all of these cranial nerves results in the failure of one or both eyes to rotate in concert with the other eye.
  • The primary symptom is diplopia caused by misalignment of the visual axes, and the pattern of Image separation is the key to diagnosing which particular ocular motor cranial nerve (and extraocular muscle) is involved.
  • With unilateral third cranial nerve palsy (i.e., oculomotor nerve palsy), the involved eye usually is deviated "down and out" (i.e., infraducted and abducted), and there may be partial or complete ptosis. In addition, pupillary dilatation can cause anisocoria (greater in the light), symptomatic glare in bright light, and accommodation deficit that may cause blurred vision for near objects.



Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 433

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following represents the third cranial nerve?
questions.solutionHtml:
Both A and C
  • Both C and A represent the superior and inferior division of the oculomotor nerve, respectively.
